answer: In this PoA design, identity verification uses a Wesolowski VDF: a domain-separated challenge—walnut, hollow, or ripple—commits each identity to a fixed chain of modular squarings, with every result required as the next input. Because the chain is inherently sequential, an attacker cannot collapse its work or parallelize a single clone across GPUs; multiple clones require proportionally separate resources, imposing a strict physical time bottleneck.
